monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes I built feel less like stone and more like paper. I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor again, trusting the lean to hold while the air above presses like a wet lid. My last moments felt heavy with worry about a roof I cannot feel, and now I want to ground that floating weight once more. The Pressed Stone sits right in the center, waiting for me to decide if the slip is tired or just waiting for permission to slide. I trace the edge of the tall rock, feeling the card's busy hum vibrate against my memory of a round stone from an older life. I will press down harder, soft and sure, letting the anchor find its peace under this sudden warmth.
